questions: Did line_loss_events fall to zero or near zero compared with iteration 0 (about 1 per run)?
Did max_error stay below 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom, and where on the track did the largest excursions occur?
Did the outer sensors (x = ±0.06) read a linear signal, or do they saturate when the tape is near the edge of the span?
Is steering_oscillation higher with seven sensors, which would suggest the signal gain is now too large at the edges?
If the robot still ends off track with no line loss, is the limit now turn authority (wheel_track) rather than sensing?

intent: Widen the sensor row from ±0.04 m to ±0.06 m (seven sensors, 0.02 m spacing, 12 mm footprints, y = 0.04 m) so the tape is still detected beyond the 0.06 m off-track limit. Everything else is held constant to isolate the effect. Expected result: fewer line-loss events and lower max_error, so more runs finish on the oval and s-bend instead of ending off track.
learning: Iteration 0 showed that off-track failure coincides with sensor coverage loss at about ±0.058 m, not with a controller gain problem. The next test checks whether extending the sensor span to ±0.066 m removes line loss and reduces max_error. If line loss persists with a wider span, the cause lies elsewhere (for example speed or turn authority).
rationale: The race evidence for iteration 0 is clear. Every s-bend and slalom trial, and 19 of 20 oval trials, ended off track, with max_error about 0.0626 m. That is just above the off-track limit, which for this body is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06 m. Widening the body cannot raise that limit meaningfully: body_width of 0.18 gives max(0.06, 0.0575), so the limit stays at 0.06 m. The robot therefore has to be kept closer to the line. The line-loss events (about 1 per run) point to the cause. The five sensors span x = ±0.04 m. Each footprint is 12 mm, so coverage reaches about ±0.046 m, and the tape (half-width 0.0125 m) is lost once its centre passes about 0.058 m. That is effectively the same as the off-track boundary. The sensors therefore lose the tape at the same moment the robot leaves the track, and there is no recovery margin. The fix is to widen the sensor row so that the tape stays visible at offsets well past where the robot would otherwise go off track. I will use seven sensors at x = ±0.06, ±0.04, ±0.02, 0, spaced 0.02 m apart with the same 12 mm footprint and y = 0.04. Coverage then extends to about ±0.066 m, which gives roughly 6 mm of margin beyond the 0.06 m limit. Adjacent footprints still overlap, so the signal remains continuous across the tape. I am keeping the forward offset, wheel track, wheel radius, body and mass unchanged. This isolates the sensor-span change, so the next race can attribute any change in line_loss_events or max_error to it. I expect line_loss_events to fall toward 0 and max_error to drop below 0.06 on oval and s-bend, which should convert some off-track ends into completions. Speed and gains are the Integrator's responsibility; I am not specifying them.
